final_message:
I fixed the bug in `render_invoice` in `billing/render.py`. The tax row was never added to the invoice text.

The function worked out the tax label and whether the tax was inclusive, but then hit a stray `pass` and never wrote a line. It now adds a "Tax (8.25%)" row with the invoice's tax total. For inclusive-priced lines it appends " included" to the label, since that tax is already part of the total.

The full suite passes (25 tests), including your reproduction test. I saved that test as `tests/test_render_invoice.py`. I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "render.py", "function": "render_invoice"}`.

I didn't commit anything.

steps.command: cat billing/render.py; cat billing/tax.py; ls billing

echo '{"file": "render.py", "function": "render_invoice"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_render_invoice.py <<'EOF'
from billing.render import render_invoice


def test_render_invoice(world):
    from billing import tax

    tax.set_tax_rate(world.ctx, "US-CA", 825, "CA")
    cus = world.customer(region="US-CA")
    world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    text = render_invoice(world.ctx, inv)
    assert "Invoice INV-00001" in text
    assert "Tax (8.25%)" in text
    assert "$10.82" in text
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
